questions.question: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some vegetables are fruits. Some fruits are flowers. All flowers are garlands. Conclusions: I. Some garlands are fruits. II. Some vegetables are flowers. III. Some vegetables are garlands.
questions.questionHtml:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

Statements:
Some vegetables are fruits.
Some fruits are flowers.
All flowers are garlands.

Conclusions:
I. Some garlands are fruits.
II. Some vegetables are flowers.
III. Some vegetables are garlands.

options.text: Only conclusions I and II follow
options.html: Only conclusions I and II follow

options.text: Only conclusions II and III follow
options.html: Only conclusions II and III follow

options.text: Only conclusions I and III follow
options.html: Only conclusions I and III follow

questions.solution:
Conclusions:

I. Some garlands are fruits → Follow (As some fruits are flowers and all flowers are garlands. As some part of fruits is common with flowers which whole comes in garlands, therefore it is true.)

II. Some vegetables are flowers → Does not follow (As some vegetables are fruits and some fruits are flowers. So it is possible but not definite.)

III. Some vegetables are garlands → Does not follow (As some vegetables are fruits, some fruits are flowers and all flowers are garlands. So it is possible but not definite.)

∴ Here, Only conclusion I follows.

questions.question: The same operation(s) are followed in all the given number pairs except one. Find that odd number pair. (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.questionHtml:
The same operation(s) are followed in all the given number pairs except one. Find that odd number pair.
(NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent
digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1
and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.solution:
Option 2) 11 : 121

(11 × 2) + 1 = 121

22 + 1 = 121

23 ≠ 121 (LHS ≠ RHS)

Thus, out of all the options '11 : 121' is the odd one out.

questions.question: Which number will come in the place of the question mark (?) in the following equation if ‘+’ and ‘−’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 27 × 3 + 4 ÷ 2 − 7 = ?
questions.questionHtml:
Which number will come in the place of the question mark (?) in the following equation if ‘+’ and ‘−’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged?
27 × 3 + 4 ÷ 2 − 7 = ?
questions.solution:
Given equation: 27 × 3 + 4 ÷ 2 - 7 = ?

Now, if ‘+’ and ‘-‘ and ‘×' and '÷’ are interchanged, then:

⇒ 27 ÷ 3 - 4 × 2 + 7 = ? ⇒ 9 - 8 + 7 = ? ⇒ 16 - 8  = 8
